proposal.summary:
Both winners verified real/unarchived/active via gh api 2026-09-26: dagu (github.com/dagucloud/dagu, pin v2.16.6) and data-pandera (github.com/unionai-oss/pandera, pin v0.33.1). Cross-checked the workflow's conv/layers.json extract against the repo's own catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json — consistent; the extract is a faithful derivation, not a fabricated citation (resolves a false-positive in the input packet's adversarial pass, which searched for a literal file named "layers.json" inside the repo checkout and found none).

PANDERA earns_it. Pin v0.33.1 is bit-for-bit current: gh api releases/latest and PyPI both show v0.33.1, GitHub published_at and PyPI upload_time both 2026-09-01 (independently verified, not just cited). Its fail-closed gate has now run against one real bounded Alpaca ingest — 24 symbols, 20 sessions, 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-22, 480 rows, 12/12 checks passing — gating one real paper trial on 2026-09-24 (gates-20260922.json "snapshot-promotion-gate" note and blueprints/us-equities/data/fixtures/good-gate-result.json, both read directly). That is more than the layer's own open_gaps text still says ("synthetic fixtures only" — stale). Its strongest challenger, Great Expectations (github.com/fivetran/great_expectations; genuine org-transfer from great-expectations/great_expectations confirmed independently via gh api, matching repo id 103071520, and separately by this repo's own manifest), was already source-reviewed by this repo's 2026-09-23 sota-convergence manifest (read directly, not just the packet's quotes) and correctly held back as heavier with "no demonstrated need," naming the exact unexecuted overturn test. I found no new evidence to overturn that.

DAGU is challenged, narrowly, on one axis. Upstream itself is healthy (4117 stars, GPL-3.0, pushed 2026-09-25) but the pin is 3 releases behind latest v2.17.2/2026-09-25 (independently reconfirmed via gh api, not just the packet's stale v2.17.0 citation), and manifest-20260923.json already names re-qualifying it on the newer release as a still-open internal action item. More structurally: this layer's requirement text explicitly asks for "recoverable state," and the same manifest cites a dedicated pin-qualification record (evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/pins-runtime/dagu.json) stating Dagu's in-flight self-healing is "inconclusive because no scheduler was started" — untested, not passed. That manifest independently names three real, current, verified Dagu alternatives targeting exactly this gap that were NOT in my input candidate packet: Nukesor/pueue, windmill-labs/windmill, and dbos-inc/dbos-transact-py. My input packet's own candidate, temporalio/temporal, targets the identical gap with full durable-execution semantics at higher operational cost. All four are real/current/verified but untested on this stack — none has actually beaten Dagu in a bounded trial yet, so this is a scoped, evidence-grounded challenge to register and test, not a replacement recommendation.

Five packet candidates — purged-cross-validation (PyPI name "purgedcv," v0.1.8 uploaded 2026-09-26, verified; JOSS paper + CITATION.cff confirmed present via direct repo-contents listing), factor-qc (PyPI v0.1.3 confirmed; DSR/PBO/Harvey-Liu claims verbatim-confirmed), quantraunak/leakprobe (README fetched directly, upgrading it from the packet's own "metadata only" to source_review: the 9/9 headline is real but is an unreleased/untagged improvement over the PyPI-published v0.1.0, which the same README says scored only 6/9 — a reproducibility gap the packet missed because it never opened the README), HephaestLab/TraderHarness (README + LICENSE fetched directly, confirming Apache-2.0 despite GitHub's NOASSERTION metadata, and confirming its own smoke-test caveat verbatim), and the arXiv paper "A Grammar of Machine Learning Workflows" (arxiv.org/abs/2603.10742, confirmed real via direct fetch, with a live matching PyPI package "mlw" and github.com/epagogy/ml) — are all genuinely real and evidenced, but every one answers a DIFFERENT, already-documented gap: this stack's own research-factors-ml and portfolio-risk layers state, verbatim and independently in both (catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, read directly), "WalkForward purge and embargo default to zero... development labels can cross fold boundaries." That is exactly what these tools exist to catch. None addresses THIS layer's actual requirement (process supervision, telemetry, recoverable state, broker-execution-authority isolation for research workers). Rejecting all five here as off-requirement and flagging them for research-factors-ml/portfolio-risk instead, where a real, already-recorded gap already names the trial they would close.

Ray, pydantic and dbt-labs/dbt were independently reconfirmed real/current/maintained via gh api but each is a different sub-capability already catalogued elsewhere (Ray→"ray-serve"), complementary not competing (pydantic), or adjacent SQL tooling with its own unresolved internal version-track ambiguity (dbt) — all correctly self-assessed as partial fits by the packet itself. Checked evidence/artifacts/alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926/ for relevance (README.md, landscape.json, tavily-research-pro.json all present, dated 2026-09-26) — its content did not surface in any dagu/pandera/dagster/temporal/prefect/great_expectations grep, so it appears scoped to market-data/execution-broker layers, not this one; not read in full.

winner_status.note: Upstream healthy (4117 stars, GPL-3.0, pushed 2026-09-25, gh api verified) but pin is 3 releases behind latest v2.17.2/2026-09-25 (gh api releases/latest, independently verified). manifest-20260923.json already names re-qualifying the pin as a still-open action item, and separately cites a dedicated pin-qualification record marking Dagu's in-flight self-healing 'inconclusive because no scheduler was started' -- the layer's own 'recoverable state' requirement is untested, not passed. Four real, current, verified alternatives (Temporal, DBOS, Windmill, Pueue) target exactly that gap; none has run on this stack.

Pin v0.33.1 exactly matches upstream latest on GitHub and PyPI (2026-09-01, independently verified). Fail-closed gate now exercised on one real bounded Alpaca ingest (24 symbols/20 sessions) gating a real paper trial on 2026-09-24 (gates-20260922.json, read directly) -- more than the layer's own open_gaps text claims. Strongest challenger (Great Expectations) already source-reviewed and correctly held back by this repo's own 2026-09-23 manifest pending one specific unexecuted seeded-defect trial; no new evidence found to overturn that.

challengers.name: Temporal (temporalio/temporal + temporalio Python SDK)
challengers.why_better: Durable execution / automatic checkpoint-replay is a real, verified core primitive that resumes in-flight workflows across crashes -- directly on the axis (recoverable state) this repo's own dedicated Dagu pin-qualification record marks 'inconclusive,' not passed.
challengers.trial_plan: Install pinned server v1.32.0 + temporalio SDK 1.33.0 (both independently verified current, 2026-09-26). Reimplement the already-qualified 3-step bounded workflow from blueprints/us-equities/hosting/receipt.json as a Temporal workflow; kill the worker mid-step-2; confirm resume from the exact interrupted step with zero duplicated broker/model calls, judged on the same failure/cancellation/output/identity/usage contract the layer's overturn_when clause names. Pass: resume beats or matches Dagu's own recorded failed/aborted/retained-history behavior on an equivalent induced failure. Overturn/reject if no specified long-running or host-loss-recovery requirement currently justifies the added server+persistence-store operational surface.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none directly (infrastructure reliability); would protect an in-progress run's recoverable state rather than add to engines run / paper acts passed / paper fills.
sources: https://github.com/temporalio/temporal (gh api, checked 2026-09-26: MIT, 23303 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-26)

challengers.name: DBOS (dbos-inc/dbos-transact-py)
challengers.why_better: This repo's own 2026-09-23 manifest -- not my input packet -- already names DBOS as resuming 'from the exact interrupted step with no duplicated side effects versus dagu/systemd's coarser whole-task restart,' a lighter Postgres-backed alternative to a full Temporal server for the same gap.
challengers.trial_plan: Stand up local Postgres; reimplement the same bounded workflow as DBOS @DBOS.workflow steps; induce the identical mid-step failure; measure step-level resume with no duplicated side effects; record the added Postgres dependency and code-restructuring cost against the benefit, per the manifest's own comparison framing. Pass: step resumes with no duplicate broker/model calls. Overturn/reject if the required code restructuring is too invasive versus Dagu's zero-code-change YAML wrapping.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none directly; same infrastructure-reliability rationale as Temporal at lower operational weight.

challengers.name: Windmill (windmill-labs/windmill)
challengers.why_better: Already named in this repo's own manifest as a direct Dagu competitor for workflows needing real polyglot application code rather than shell/SSH/container steps in a static YAML DAG, with its own named comparison test.
challengers.trial_plan: Per the manifest's own comparison_that_would_overturn: run the same frozen local-workload fixtures under Windmill, measuring cancel-to-stop latency and step-recovery behavior after a killed worker, against Dagu on the identical workload, including the added Postgres+worker footprint Windmill requires that Dagu's single static binary avoids. Overturn/reject if that footprint isn't justified, or if the licensing concern below isn't resolved.
sources: https://github.com/windmill-labs/windmill (gh api, checked 2026-09-26: license field NOASSERTION, 18035 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-26)

catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260923.json (Windmill fit/comparison text, and a separate note that CE binaries include proprietary code that bars wrapping -- license needs a direct LICENSE-file read before adoption, not done this pass)

challengers.name: Pueue (Nukesor/pueue)
challengers.why_better: Already named in this repo's own manifest as a lighter Dagu alternative that 'sidesteps the open gap that Dagu upstream v2.17.0 is newer than the accepted 2.16.6 pin and has not been re-qualified'; Apache-2.0 (cleaner than Dagu's GPL-3.0, though GPL-3.0 is low-stakes for this stack's private internal use).
challengers.trial_plan: Per the manifest's own comparison_that_would_overturn: run the same frozen local-workload fixtures under Pueue, measuring pueue kill cancellation latency and whether daemon-restart truly recovers persisted history, against Dagu on the identical workload.
sources: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue (gh api, checked 2026-09-26: Apache-2.0, 6352 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-09)

challengers.name: Dagster
challengers.why_better: Asset-centric model puts data-quality checks as graph nodes next to the assets they gate, matching this layer's own overturn_when trigger for 'asset/backfill lineage' -- the escalation condition this candidate maps to most literally. Pin 1.13.24 is current, independently reconfirmed against upstream.
challengers.trial_plan: Model the existing Pandera-gated daily-bar ingest (blueprints/us-equities/data/ingest_snapshot.py) as a Dagster software-defined asset with the Pandera check as an attached asset check; run a backfill over the same 24-symbol/20-session window already exercised in trial adaptive-20260923g; compare lineage/backfill bookkeeping against the current bespoke script. Pass: reproduces the same 12/12-check gate result while adding queryable lineage/backfill history the current setup lacks. Overturn/reject if no concrete backfill/lineage requirement currently justifies the added webserver+daemon+metadata-DB footprint.
sources: https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster (gh api, checked 2026-09-26: Apache-2.0, 16202 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-25)

challengers.name: Great Expectations
challengers.why_better: Larger expectation-suite feature set and community than Pandera; genuine org transfer confirmed independently (same repo id 103071520 under both slugs). Not yet shown better in practice -- this repo's own 2026-09-23 manifest already ran this exact comparison and held it back.
challengers.trial_plan: Per this repo's own manifest: run Pandera's current gate and a Great Expectations 1.23.2 suite against the same real snapshot the licensed-vendor/SEC pull already produces (today only exercises Pandera on a synthetic 4-row CSV), with deliberately planted eligibility violations. Measure (1) whether each fails closed on an unknown/out-of-window record, (2) whether GE catches a defect Pandera's ~12-dependency check misses on a real record, (3) added code/dependency cost versus the existing DuckDB+Pandera pipeline. Pass criterion for keeping Pandera: a custom Pandera check achieves the same fail-closed + auditable outcome for materially less added complexity. Overturn: GE catches a concrete defect class Pandera misses.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: indirect at best (could prevent a bad snapshot from passing the gate and reaching a paper act/fill); no evidence yet that this has happened -- none until the trial runs.
sources: https://github.com/fivetran/great_expectations (gh api, checked 2026-09-26: Apache-2.0, 11844 stars, pushed_at 2026-09-25, repo id 103071520 matches old great-expectations/great_expectations slug)
https://pypi.org/pypi/great-expectations/json (1.23.2, uploaded 2026-09-25 -- one patch ahead of the latest tagged GitHub Release)

rejected.name: Apache Airflow
rejected.reason: Real, current (v3.3.2, 2026-09-17, independently verified), genuinely absent from this repo's whole catalog (coverage.json/repository-index.md/landscape json all zero hits for 'airflow', confirmed by direct grep) despite Dagu's own GitHub description self-describing as an 'Alternative to Airflow' (verified verbatim via gh api). A real catalog gap worth recording, but no verified evidence it closes a concrete gap Dagu leaves open at this stack's current bounded/local scope; heavier scheduler+webserver+metadata-DB footprint than the layer's stated scope. Register as known-but-not-prioritized.

rejected.name: Prefect
rejected.reason: Real, current (v3.8.6, 2026-09-14/15, independently verified via gh api release tag + PyPI). Pure-Python workflow definitions are a genuine ergonomic advantage over Dagu's YAML DAG, but no specific documented Dagu gap (unlike recoverable-state or asset lineage) points to Prefect specifically. Already tagged 'agents-operations: alternative / already_covered' in this repo's own repository-index.md. Register as known-but-not-prioritized.

rejected.name: Ray
rejected.reason: Real, current, heavily maintained (43929 stars, pushed 2026-09-26, independently verified), but this repo's coverage.json already catalogues ray-project/ray under catalog_entry_id 'ray-serve' -- a different sub-capability (model serving) than the packet's actual framing (general actor/task fan-out). The packet's own fit note admits full fault-tolerance claims need a docs-level, not README-level, read. Off-requirement as framed.

rejected.name: pydantic
rejected.reason: Real, current, independently verified (28884 stars, pushed 2026-09-25). Row/object-level type validation is complementary to, not competitive with, Pandera's dataframe-level statistical gate. Off-requirement as a Pandera substitute.

rejected.name: dbt (dbt-labs/dbt / dbt-core)
rejected.reason: Real, current, independently verified (13933 stars, pushed 2026-09-26). Covers SQL-transform testing/lineage, adjacent to a DuckDB SQL layer that doesn't exist at that scale yet, not a substitute for either current winner. Also carries an unresolved internal ambiguity the packet itself flagged: the dbt-labs/dbt meta-repo's GitHub tag (v2.0.5) and the dbt-core PyPI engine package (1.12.5) are on diverging version tracks -- needs disambiguation before any pin.

rejected.name: purged-cross-validation / purgedcv
rejected.reason: Genuinely well-evidenced and current (PyPI name 'purgedcv' v0.1.8 uploaded 2026-09-26, matching the GitHub release exactly; JOSS paper and CITATION.cff confirmed present via direct repo-contents listing). Off-requirement for data-quality-orchestration specifically: answers 'does my cross-validation leak future information,' which this stack's own research-factors-ml and portfolio-risk layers already name, verbatim and independently in both, as an open gap ('WalkForward purge and embargo default to zero'). Recommend registering it there instead.

rejected.name: factor-qc
rejected.reason: Real (PyPI v0.1.3 confirmed; DSR/PBO/Harvey-Liu/MinTRL claims and its own 'battle-tested... self-reported' language verbatim-confirmed via direct README read), but 0 GitHub stars, single-maintainer, no independent adopters found. Off-requirement for this layer for the same reason as purged-cross-validation -- belongs near research-factors-ml/evaluation-experiments, not process-supervision/telemetry.

rejected.name: leakprobe
rejected.reason: Upgraded from the packet's 'metadata only' rating to source_review by directly fetching its README this pass: the 9-of-9 catch-rate headline is real but is an unreleased/untagged improvement over the PyPI-published v0.1.0, which the same README says scored only 6 of 9 -- a real reproducibility gap. 0 stars, unreleased. Off-requirement for this layer.

rejected.name: HephaestLab/TraderHarness
rejected.reason: Real and well-built; its smoke-test caveat verbatim-confirmed via direct README fetch, and its LICENSE file directly confirms Apache-2.0 despite GitHub metadata showing NOASSERTION. Off-requirement today: shipped dataset is China A-share only with no US-equities adapter (this stack's explicit north star), and its design lets the LLM agent both decide and place its own simulated orders inside one harness, unlike this stack's deliberate separation of research (models) from execution (the deterministic adaptive-paper engine only). Interesting prior art for point-in-time masking, not a fit today.

rejected.name: A Grammar of Machine Learning Workflows (mlw / ml, arXiv:2603.10742)
rejected.reason: Confirmed real via direct fetch (Simon Roth, v1 2026-03-11 / v4 2026-05-29, cs.LG) with a matching live PyPI package ('mlw' v1.1.2) and GitHub repo (epagogy/ml, MIT). Off-requirement for this layer: a call-time-enforced evaluate/assess-boundary grammar for ML methodology, closer to research-factors-ml's concerns. Also the quietest upstream checked this pass -- last pushed 2026-05-24, about four months before this review; not yet over the 12-month unmaintained threshold but worth watching.

claude_verify_checks.name: top8-selection-method
claude_verify_checks.claim: Which 8 of the 15 supplied candidates count as 'top 8 by fit' (the packet does not pre-rank them).
claude_verify_checks.note: This is a researcher judgment call, not a checkable fact. I ranked by how unhedged each candidate's own 'fit' paragraph is: Dagster, Apache Airflow, Temporal, Prefect, Great Expectations, purged-cross-validation, factor-qc and TraderHarness all claim a direct/structural fit. Excluded as weaker/hedged fits: Ray ('needs a docs-level read before promotion'), pydantic ('only partly right... complementary rather than head-to-head'), dbt ('partial, adjacent fit... not a substitute'), leakprobe (metadata-only, README not opened by the original researcher), the mlw/ml paper (general-ML, not finance-specific, quiet upstream), Apache Hamilton ('confirmed weak fit... not an orchestrator' by its own README), and pypbo (metadata-only, superseded framing, AGPL friction). All 8 selected candidates were adversarially checked below.

researched_candidates.name: Dagster
researched_candidates.fit: Dagster's asset-centric model fuses this layer's two separately-adopted winners (Dagu for orchestration, Pandera for validation) into one graph where data-quality checks are nodes next to the assets they gate -- structurally closer to 'supervise owned processes... retain... recoverable state' than a pure task-runner. Apache-2.0 (vs Dagu's GPL-3.0) is a licensing plus. Against it: heavier deployment (webserver+daemon+DB) than Dagu's single static binary -- exactly the profile Dagu's own README targets ('teams whose main work isn't orchestration'); no native run on this stack exists, so this is documented, not demonstrated.

researched_candidates.name: Apache Airflow
researched_candidates.fit: The incumbent industry-standard workflow scheduler, and conspicuously absent from this repository's own catalog (no 'airflow' hit in coverage.json or repository-index.md) despite Dagu's own README self-describing as an 'Alternative to Airflow / Cron / Job Scheduler' -- the stack adopted a lightweight Dagu without a recorded comparison against the incumbent it explicitly positions against. Genuine catalog gap. Against adoption: Airflow's scheduler+webserver+metadata-DB footprint is heavy relative to the layer's stated 'bounded... local command workflows' scope, and nothing here shows it closes a concrete gap Dagu leaves open.

researched_candidates.name: Temporal
researched_candidates.fit: Of every workflow engine checked, Temporal's core primitive -- automatic checkpoint/replay of in-progress workflow state across crashes -- maps most literally onto this layer's own requirement wording ('supervise owned processes; retain... recoverable state'), closer than Dagu's completed-history-only restart (layers.json's own gap: Dagu's 'completed-history restart is not recovery of in-flight work'). The concrete next step this stack's own materials already imply: one bounded local Temporal workflow with an induced mid-run failure, compared against Dagu on the same failure/cancellation/output contract per this layer's overturn_when clause.

researched_candidates.name: Prefect
researched_candidates.fit: Supplied as a starred-repo input already marked in_catalog:true elsewhere in this stack's catalog; converges again here as a Python-native (workflow logic in the same language as the research code it supervises, unlike Dagu's YAML DSL) alternative with first-class retries/caching/event triggers. Strongest pure-Python orchestration candidate, at the cost of a heavier server/DB deployment than Dagu's single binary.

researched_candidates.name: Ray
researched_candidates.fit: Matches the input packet's own framing exactly: a general distributed actor/task substrate for supervising bounded parallel research workers with retries, rather than a DAG/YAML scheduler like Dagu. Weaker than Dagster/Airflow/Temporal/Prefect for host-loss recovery (Ray's fault tolerance is opt-in and cluster-lifecycle-bound, not durable-execution-by-default), but a stronger fit for fine-grained fan-out of many short-lived research-worker tasks with backpressure/retry -- closer to this stack's actual Ultracode-style worker pattern than a cron-like DAG. Full fault-tolerance claims need a docs-level (not README-level) read before promotion.

researched_candidates.name: Great Expectations
researched_candidates.fit: Direct Pandera competitor with a larger community and richer tooling, but already source-reviewed and provisionally rejected by this stack's own prior convergence pass as unnecessary weight given Pandera already backs an established fail-closed snapshot-promotion gate -- confirmed firsthand in catalogs/us-equities/gates-20260922.json lines 68-83, which also shows a real (not only synthetic) 24-symbol/20-session Alpaca ingest passed that gate on 2026-09-24, more current than the 'synthetic fixtures only' framing in layers.json's own gaps text. Merit verdict: keep Pandera unless the named seeded-defect comparison shows GX catching something it misses.

researched_candidates.name: pydantic
researched_candidates.fit: Validates Python objects/dicts against type-hinted schemas -- a different primary object model from Pandera's dataframe/column statistical checks. The input packet's framing ('same role as the adopted Pandera') is only partly right: Pandera can itself use pydantic models as an underlying schema layer in recent releases, making these complementary rather than head-to-head substitutes. Fits as a row-level/config-object validation layer alongside Pandera's dataframe-level gate, not a replacement.

researched_candidates.name: dbt
researched_candidates.fit: Covers SQL-transform testing/lineage rather than Python dataframe validation or process orchestration -- a partial, adjacent fit for a pipeline whose DuckDB layer grows SQL-modeled transforms that want declarative tests alongside Pandera's Python-side gate. Not a substitute for either current winner.

researched_candidates.name: purged-cross-validation
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest-evidenced tool in the quant-specific leakage/overfitting-gate niche: real algorithmic breadth in one sklearn-compatible package, a release literally dated the day of this research (v0.1.8, 2026-09-26), and a JOSS submission absent from every other niche candidate. Extends what Pandera's gate does not do -- Pandera checks schema/values, this checks whether a cross-validation split itself leaks future information into training -- a genuine capability gap, not a redundant reimplementation. Older, more battle-tested but AGPL-3.0-licensed prior art for the same math exists (esvhd/pypbo, separately listed).

researched_candidates.name: factor-qc
researched_candidates.fit: The most statistically comprehensive single fail-closed gate found for backtest-overfitting detection (DSR+PBO+Harvey-Liu+MinTRL in one tool); its P0/P1/P2 exit-code contract is a close structural match to a CI-style orchestration gate. Against it: zero GitHub stars, a two-repo single-maintainer org with no independent adopters found, and the 'battle-tested' claim is self-reported with no named external user. A promising, unadopted, single-maintainer tool, not yet SOTA by community validation.

researched_candidates.name: leakprobe
researched_candidates.fit: Addresses a genuinely different sub-problem than the PBO/DSR tools: checking whether the feature-pipeline code itself leaks future information, rather than auditing a backtest's results after the fact -- complements rather than duplicates factor-qc/purged-cross-validation. Notable convergence: this and holdout-labs/lookahead-free were created within about three weeks of each other (2026-08-18 and 2026-09-10) with near-identical framing, suggesting multiple small teams are independently discovering this specific capability gap right now. Zero stars, unreleased, and the headline catch-rate claim came from a search snippet, not a verified README -- needs a direct source_review before real weight is placed on it.

researched_candidates.name: TraderHarness
researched_candidates.fit: The candidate whose stated purpose most literally matches this layer's own requirement text -- 'native identity and complete returned results... without granting research workers broker execution authority' is essentially what point-in-time masking, anonymization and fingerprinted replay exist to guarantee for an LLM research worker, directly relevant to how this stack already uses Claude/Codex as research workers. Held back by: A-share-only data today (a US-equities adapter would need building), and a benchmark the authors themselves label a smoke test, not a validated result.

researched_candidates.name: A Grammar of Machine Learning Workflows: Rejecting Data Leakage at Call Time (mlw / ml)
researched_candidates.fit: General-purpose ML methodology, not finance-specific, but directly on point for this layer's own requirement language around complete, recoverable, non-leaking research results -- a call-time structural constraint is a stronger guarantee than any post-hoc statistical or metamorphic checker above. Against adoption: the reference-implementation repo (epagogy/ml) has only 9 stars and was last pushed 2026-05-24, over four months before this check -- quieter than any finance-specific tool above, and integrating a general-ML grammar into a trading-specific pipeline would itself be nontrivial engineering. Marked maintained:false on that 4+ month push-silence signal, though it is still under the 12-month archival threshold.

researched_candidates.name: Apache Hamilton (incubating)
researched_candidates.fit: Confirmed weak fit for this layer's process-supervision half by the project's own README ('not an orchestrator'), but a real, actively-developed dataflow/lineage/testability layer that could sit inside an orchestrator (Dagu, Dagster, Airflow, Temporal, Prefect) rather than replace one. The ASF-incubation move is a genuine positive governance signal worth tracking, but the release process is still incubating-RC only, not a stable GA cadence.

researched_candidates.name: pypbo
researched_candidates.fit: The oldest and most-starred prior art for this exact niche, valuable as the baseline every newer tool should be checked against for correctness of the underlying statistics. AGPL-3.0 is a materially more restrictive copyleft license than every other MIT/Apache candidate here -- AGPL's network-use disclosure trigger is normally not implicated by a local, non-networked research library, but it is a real legal-review item this stack has not needed for any other adopted component, and is a concrete reason a newer MIT-licensed reimplementation (purged-cross-validation) may be preferable even if statistically equivalent.
